author: agent
question: What if your music app had no ads, no account, and nothing left to sell you?

inspiration.note: 3.5x channel-median outlier. Taken as lead only: proof-in-frame-one timing, one emphasised keyword per caption phrase, claim→mechanism→breadth→caveat beat order. Their browser-mock framing, yellow-pill captions, mascot end card and every script sentence stay theirs. See research/references/tiktok-github.signals-7706422892908662034/teardown.md

hook_visual.intent: player UI already on screen at t=0 (proof in frame one, per teardown); the three removals light up one by one as said

points.claim: A server you run fetches the stream with yt-dlp and hands the bytes to the player.
points.spoken: A small server that you run fetches the stream itself and hands it to the player — that is why there is nothing to skip.
points.source_note: README 'What it is': 'No ads, no account: the server gets the original stream with yt-dlp and passes the bytes to the player.'

visual.intent: mechanism row: your computer runs the server, the server fetches, the player just plays

points.title: It fetches the stream itself
points.sub: A server you run gets the stream with yt-dlp and passes it to the player.

points.claim: Audio and video switch mid-track from the same position, and songs get the artist's official music video.
points.spoken: Flip between audio and video mid-song, from the same second — for songs it even finds the artist's official music video.
points.source_note: README 'What it is': 'Song or music video: switch between Audio and Video at any time, from the same point in the track. For songs, Musike finds the artist's official music video.'

visual.intent: audio/video toggle on a playing track, time marker stays put, video frame appears

points.title: Audio becomes video mid-song
points.sub: The switch happens at the same second, and songs get their official music video.

points.claim: It runs as Windows, macOS and Linux apps, Android, Android TV and iPhone apps, an installable browser PWA, and a Docker image.
points.spoken: Desktop, phone, TV, browser, Docker — the same player runs on all of them, and the phone app needs no computer.
points.source_note: README intro paragraph: 'Runs as a Windows, macOS and Linux app, as an Android, Android TV and iPhone app that needs no computer, in any browser (installable PWA) and in Docker.'

visual.intent: breadth stack: three rows of platform chips light up in sync with the list

points.title: One player, every screen
points.sub: Desktop, mobile, TV, browser PWA and Docker — the phone app needs no computer.

points.claim: Playlists and favorites live in a local file you can export and move to any other Musike.
points.spoken: Your playlists and favourites stay in a local file you can export — take your whole library to any other install.
points.source_note: README 'What it is' 'Yours' bullet: 'Playlists and favorites live in a local file you can export and take to any other Musike.' + Contents: 'Moving your library (backup)'.

visual.intent: library card slides into a file icon, file copies itself to a second device

points.title: Your library is a file
points.sub: Export playlists and favourites, and carry them to any other Musike.
steps: Library lives in a local file
Load it on any other Musike

catch: It is for personal use: the README says playing YouTube streams without ads breaks YouTube's terms, and public bots like Groovy and Rythm were shut down after notices from Google.
catch_sub: Personal use only — public services doing this were shut down before.

steps: Groovy and Rythm were shut down
catch_visual.intent: the honest limit card: README legal notice as three sober rows

cta: Would you run your own music player? Comment MUSIKE and I'll pin the repo link.

youtube.title: Musike Runs on 8 Platforms and Charges Nothing
youtube.description: Musike is an open-source music player for YouTube's catalog. A server you run fetches the stream with yt-dlp, so playback has no ads, no account and no subscription. Audio and video switch mid-track, it runs on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, Android TV, iPhone, as a browser PWA and in Docker, and your playlists and favourites live in a local file you can export. Personal use only — the README's legal notice explains YouTube's terms. Repo: https://github.com/Ernani1234/musike #Shorts #Musike #OpenSource #MusicPlayer #SelfHosted

tiktok.caption: Musike plays YouTube's catalog with no ads, no account and no subscription — you run the server yourself. Open source. Personal use only.

instagram.caption: An open-source music player with no ads, no account and no subscription. You run the server; it even switches audio to video mid-song. Personal use only.

facebook.caption: Musike: run a tiny local server and play YouTube's music catalog with no ads and no account. Open source, personal use only.

x.text: Musike: an open-source player for YouTube's catalog — no ads, no account, no subscription. You run the server. Personal use only.

brief_meta.title: Musike: an open-source music player with nothing to sell you
brief_meta.idea: Musike plays YouTube's catalog with no ads, account or subscription because a server you run fetches the stream; it switches audio to video mid-song, runs on every screen, and keeps your library in a file you own.

viewer.who: listeners tired of ads inside music apps, who like self-hosting open-source tools
viewer.problem: mainstream music apps push ads, accounts and subscriptions between you and the song
viewer.job: decide whether running your own small streaming server is worth it for ad-free personal playback
